title: Round numbers don't make wicks reverse more often. But buying the reclaim at one loses, and that held on five years of data I hadn't touched (pre-registered, three locked tests)
author: Huge_Position890

comments.author: Huge_Position890
comments.body:
\*\*Correction: the replication in this post doesn't survive a proper coin universe.\*\*



A Reddit comment about choosing coins by monthly volume made me look at something I should have checked before posting. All three locked tests used a fixed list of 17 large coins, and I chose that list in 2026. Looking at 2019 through it means already knowing who ends up big. The post didn't list that as a limit.



So I locked a new test before reading any return:



\- \*\*Universe:\*\* every month, the top 30 USDT spot pairs by the previous month's quote volume. Delisted coins are included (695 pairs in all, 191 dead). Stablecoins, wrapped tokens and leveraged tokens are out.

\- \*\*Dead coins:\*\* if a coin dies inside the 3-day hold, the trade exits at its last close.

\- \*\*Everything else is unchanged:\*\* same events, same definitions, same window, same one-sided rule.

\- \*\*My prediction:\*\* "replicates" 0.45, "same direction but weak" 0.35, "doesn't replicate" 0.20.



\*\*Result: it doesn't replicate.\*\*



| Near-minus-far gap, 3 days, 2019–2023 | Gap (points) | Near events |

|---|---|---|

| Fixed 17 (what I posted) | −1.40 \[−2.85, +0.02\] | 316 |

| \*\*Top 30 that month (locked)\*\* | \*\*+0.08 \[−0.96, +1.11\]\*\* | 587 |

| Same, only coins outside the fixed 17 | +0.47 \[−1.11, +1.89\] | 345 |



The interval excludes the −1.3 to −1.4 I reported. It doesn't exclude a small negative effect.



\*\*The rest of the picture:\*\*



\- \*\*2023–2026, top 30:\*\* −0.89 \[−1.78, −0.03\]. Still negative, but this window is where the pattern was found, and many of its events are the same ones.

\- \*\*All of 2019–2026, top 30:\*\* −0.33 \[−1.03, +0.37\].

\- \*\*All of 2019–2026, coins outside the fixed 17:\*\* +0.04 \[−0.90, +0.93\].

\- \*\*Scale check:\*\* the real gap beats only 20 of 39 shifted copies, nowhere near the 37 I required for calling it specific to round numbers.



\*\*Where the −1.40 came from (after the fact, not locked).\*\* The new code reproduces the old number on the old list (−1.39), so this isn't a pipeline difference. Splitting the fixed 17 by whether each coin was in that month's top 30:



\- \*\*In the top 30:\*\* −0.48 \[−1.94, +1.00\], 242 near events.

\- \*\*Not yet in the top 30:\*\* −4.46 \[−8.63, −1.15\], 74 near events.



So most of the gap comes from 74 events on coins before they got big, which is exactly the part a 2026 list picks with hindsight. Those 74 events are too few to explain, and I won't build a story on them.



\*\*The tail result flips too.\*\* I reported that only the adverse tail gets fatter.



| Beyond 2σ, near ÷ far, 2019–2026 | Adverse tail | Favourable tail |

|---|---|---|

| Fixed 17 | 1.47× (lower bound 1.09) | 0.88× |

| Top 30 that month | 1.10× (0.86) | 1.41× (1.01) |

| Coins outside the fixed 17 | 0.84× (0.53) | 1.61× (1.02) |



\*\*What's left of the post:\*\*



\- \*\*Gone:\*\* "buying the reclaim at a round number loses," "it held on five years of untouched data," and "only the adverse tail."

\- \*\*Not re-tested:\*\* "breaks reverse no more often at round numbers." That test used the same 17 coins, on 2023–2026, so it's less exposed but it has the same flaw.

\- \*\*I called the replication independent, and it wasn't.\*\* The years were new, but the list was selected the same way.



\*\*The commenter's other two points, measured:\*\*



\- \*\*Age and volatility:\*\* within the same month, among the top 100, younger coins are more volatile. Rank correlation −0.46 to −0.57 in every year from 2019 to 2026.

\- \*\*"The list barely changes anymore":\*\* not at this size. The share of the top 30 that's new each month rose from about 14% in 2019 to 32% in 2026. I didn't measure the very top of the list, where it may well be true.



From now on, any test that looks back with a fixed coin list either uses that month's universe or says so as a limit.



\*Not financial advice. This is a research log.\*

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Posting the correction at the top, with the new interval that includes zero, is the part most people skip, so respect for that. The thing I'd add is that "doesn't replicate" isn't the same as "the opposite is true". With a few hundred events the interval is still wide, so I'd treat this as unresolved rather than flipping to the other side. Since the first result came from a list chosen with hindsight, I'd also try to get one more clean stretch you never touched before reading any returns. Cymetica's Backtest Labs can hold the last 30% of history aside as out-of-sample, which fits that kind of check.
